title: Associate Scientist/Scientist I, Translational Biology
text:
Your Impact at LILA
We are seeking a driven and scientifically rigorous Associate Scientist with deep flow cytometry and cross-species tissue handling expertise to join our translational biology team. In this role, flow cytometry and ex vivo tissue processing are your core disciplines: you will independently isolate and process cells from liver, spleen, and whole blood across mouse, rat, NHP, and human samples, and execute complex multi-parameter panels to interrogate LNP uptake, cellular delivery, immune activation, and phenotypic response across in vitro and ex vivo models. Working closely with team leadership, you will help develop and refine assay strategy, contribute to experimental design, and complement this with a broader immunoassay and cell biology toolkit to evaluate lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery and therapeutic function. Beyond hands-on execution, you will interpret and contextualize data to inform project direction and partner with leadership to advance key scientific questions. You will help shape LILA's high-throughput, data-rich discovery workflows at the intersection of biology, automation, and AI, while mentoring junior team members on flow and tissue-processing technique and best practices.
What You'll Be Building
- Serve as a flow cytometry subject-matter expert: independently execute high-dimensional, multi-parameter panels to assess cell viability, LNP uptake, transfection/expression, immune activation, and marker phenotyping across primary and immortalized cell types; partner with leadership on panel design and assay development strategy.
- Own the full flow workflow: fluorophore selection and spectral considerations, compensation/unmixing, instrument setup and QC, acquisition, and rigorous analysis and interpretation in FlowJo (or spectral/conventional platform software); collaborate with leadership to develop and optimize new panels.
- Serve as a tissue processing and cell isolation expert: independently isolate viable single-cell suspensions and immune populations from liver, spleen, and whole blood across mouse, rat, NHP, and human samples, including perfusion, mechanical/enzymatic dissociation, density-gradient separation (PBMC/leukocyte), and RBC lysis; work with leadership to establish and optimize new cross-species workflows.
- Prepare and process tissues from in vitro and in vivo studies for downstream analysis (flow, ELISA, multiplex, qPCR), including homogenization, protein/RNA extraction, and lysate preparation; ensure high viability and yield for cross-species flow readouts.

We are looking to hire technical members responsible for the customer success of Matlantis, a SaaS service provided by PFCC.
With the mission of "exploring the creation of innovative materials for a sustainable world," PFCC provides Matlantis, a versatile calculation engine, to help customers accelerate the development of new materials and the elucidation of their mechanisms.
Traditionally, first-principles calculations have not been able to perform a large number of trials due to their large computational cost. In the materials industry, it is common to discover materials through experimentation first and then perform first-principles calculations to elucidate phenomena later.

- B.S., B.A., or M.S. in Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, Chemistry, or a related scientific field

- Strong documentation habits and the ability to work independently and troubleshoot calmly
- A fast learner with a scrappy, can-do attitude who wants to master new, multi-step workflows
- Genuine enthusiasm for automation and robotics; you're excited to work alongside machines

- Protein expression in mammalian (e.g., Expi293, ExpiCHO), microbial, or cell-free systems

We are looking for a Scientist to own biophysical characterization on the Medra Physical AI platform. You will develop, validate, and scale label-free binding assays — primarily SPR and BLI — and turn them into robust, high-throughput workflows that run autonomously for our customers. Antibody affinity and kinetics, epitope binning, self-interaction, and quantitation are the daily bread of this role, and you’ll be responsible for making these assays reproducible, automation-ready, and reliable at a throughput and consistency that manual benchwork can’t match.
This is a role for someone who blends deep biophysical judgment with hands-on craft — someone who has designed and run SPR/BLI campaigns in high-stakes settings and is energized by the idea of translating that expertise into an autonomous lab. You will work closely with roboticists and software engineers to bring these assays into routine execution on our platform, and directly with customers to scope and deliver characterization campaigns.
Key Responsibilities:
- Develop, validate, and run SPR and BLI assays across the full range of formats — affinity and kinetics, epitope binning, self-interaction (AC-SINS and BLI-based), and concentration/quantitation — on platforms including the Carterra LSA and Gator BLI
- Design assay strategies for antibody and alternative binder characterization, selecting the right sensor chemistry, capture approach, regeneration conditions, and analysis models for each target and format
- Build out new biophysical capabilities end-to-end: scope the need, evaluate technologies, qualify instruments, write SOPs, and prepare validated workflows for autonomous execution
- Partner with roboticists and software engineers to translate manual SPR/BLI workflows into reliable, high-throughput autonomous protocols — including sample handling, plate setup, sensor/chip management, and data pipeline integration
- Develop rigorous data analysis and QC frameworks for kinetics fitting, binning heatmaps, and developability flags, and interpret results to inform customer go/no-go decisions
- Integrate biophysical data with orthogonal characterization — thermal stability (nanoDSF/DSC), aggregation and monomericity (HPLC-SEC/DLS), and polyspecificity — to give customers an integrated developability picture
- Work directly with customers to scope characterization campaigns, communicate results clearly, and translate their scientific questions into executable assay plans
- Maintain rigorous experimental records in electronic lab notebooks (ELN) and drive reproducibility across every assay you deploy
What You Bring to the Team

- Deep hands-on expertise with SPR and/or BLI — instrument operation, assay development, and data analysis — with a track record of generating high-quality kinetics data
- Strong command of binding kinetics theory and its practical pitfalls: avidity, mass transport, regeneration, surface capacity, and fitting model selection
- Demonstrated experience developing and qualifying biophysical assays from scratch, including method validation and troubleshooting
- Working understanding of antibody structure, function, and the therapeutic antibody discovery and developability process
- Strong documentation habits, attention to detail, and the ability to drive multiple workstreams in parallel

- Experience developing developability assay panels (nanoDSF/DLS, HPLC-SEC/HIC, AC-SINS) and integrating multi-instrument datasets
- Experience building analysis pipelines or scripting for high-throughput kinetics data (Python/R)
- Track record of developing and qualifying new assays or platforms from scratch

title: Research Associate, Protein Purification & Quality Control
text:
What We’re Building
At Medra, our mission is to use AI, robotics, and biology to accelerate life science research, with the ultimate goal of eradicating disease. We have been quietly building the foundational layers of our Physical AI Scientist platform:

About the Role
We are looking for a Research Associate to help build and run protein production and quality control on the Medra Physical AI platform. Working alongside our scientists, you will execute the workflow that takes antibodies and alternative binders from cells to purified, characterized material — automated cell growth, transfection, purification, and analytical QC — and help turn these steps into robust, high-throughput workflows that run autonomously for our customers. Expression, capture and polishing chromatography, and purity and monomericity analysis are the daily bread of this role, and you’ll play a hands-on part in making them reproducible, automation-ready, and reliable.
This is a role for someone early in their career who loves being at the bench, has strong hands-on instincts, and is eager to grow their protein science under the guidance of experienced scientists. You’ll work closely with roboticists and software engineers to bring cell culture, purification, and QC into routine autonomous execution on our platform.
Key Responsibilities
• Run automated mammalian cell growth and transfection for recombinant protein expression, including cell maintenance, expansion, and transient transfection
• Perform protein purification on AKTA (FPLC) and KingFisher platforms — affinity capture, polishing, buffer exchange, and magnetic-bead-based processing
• Execute analytical QC by SEC (analytical UPLC/HPLC) to assess purity, aggregation, and monomericity, and support additional QC as needed (concentration, endotoxin, SDS-PAGE)
• Prepare buffers, resins, columns, and consumables, and carry out instrument cleaning, maintenance, and column packing/qualification to keep workflows running reliably
• Execute purification and QC according to established SOPs, and help refine and document protocols as workflows mature
• Partner with roboticists and software engineers to translate manual purification and QC steps into reliable, high-throughput autonomous protocols — including sample handling, deck/plate setup, and data pipeline integration
• Perform first-pass data analysis and QC on chromatograms and SEC traces, tracking yield and purity and flagging anomalies for review
• Maintain rigorous, well-organized experimental records in electronic lab notebooks (ELN) and support reproducibility across every batch you produce
What You Bring to the Team
• B.S. or M.S. in biochemistry, molecular biology, chemical/biological engineering, or a related discipline, with hands-on laboratory experience (research, internship, or 0–2+ years of industry/academic lab work)
• Hands-on experience with protein purification — chromatography on AKTA/FPLC and/or bead-based purification — and comfort taking a sample from lysate or supernatant to purified protein
• Hands-on wet-lab experience and comfort at the bench — mammalian cell culture, aseptic technique, pipetting, and careful execution of detailed protocols
• Curiosity about protein biochemistry and analytical characterization, and eagerness to learn the theory and practical pitfalls (aggregation, capture chemistry, buffer conditions, column behavior)
• Strong documentation habits, attention to detail, and the ability to juggle multiple tasks in parallel
• A basic understanding of antibody structure and function, or a strong desire to learn it
• A scrappy, can-do attitude — you figure things out, ask good questions, and get things done
Bonus Points For
• Hands-on experience with analytical SEC or other analytical chromatography (UPLC/HPLC)
• Experience with automated or high-throughput purification (e.g., KingFisher, multi-column AKTA, robotic purification)
• Experience with mammalian expression systems (CHO/HEK) and transient transfection at scale
• Experience with lab automation or liquid handling platforms (e.g., Dynamic Devices Lynx, Tempest)
• Familiarity with alternative binder formats — VHHs, bispecifics, Fc-fusions, or non-Ig scaffolds
• Basic scripting or data-handling skills (Python/R) for organizing and analyzing purification and QC data

Phase 2 — Establish the In-House Quality Organization (New Manufacturing Plant)
- Build the QMS: implement ISO 9001 backbone (coordinate with 14001/45001 where relevant); write SOPs/WIs, MRB/CAPA governance, document control, and e-sign workflows.
- Factory quality architecture: stand up in-process, and final test (FAT) for CDUs and modular skids; define station-level CTQs, stop-the-line criteria, etc.
- People & org: hire, train, and coach inspectors, technicians, SQEs/CQEs; set tiered daily management (tier boards, paretos, andons) and a prevention-first culture (poka-yoke, error-proof fixtures).
- Systems integration: integrate Quality with PLM/ERP/MES for single source of truth; enable digital travelers, barcoding/RFID traceability, and automated data capture from test stands.
- Ramp & readiness: plan EVT/DVT/PVT at the plant; qualify production lines/process windows; lock control plans and release criteria before rate increase.
- Compliance & certifications: secure/maintain with the required multi-departmental team members UL/CSA/CE/UKCA, EMC/LVD, UL 508A for panels, pressure equipment (ASME/PED, CRN), refrigerant handling safety, RoHS/REACH documentation.
Ongoing, Cross-Phase Responsibilities
- Reliability & field quality: track MTBF/FFR, drive failure analysis (5-Whys, fishbone, FTA), manage warranty/RMA and design/process feedback loops.
- Continuous improvement & COPQ reduction: DOE, SPC, yield improvement, and cost-of-quality tracking; implement mistake-proofing and automation.
- Risk management: multi-tier mapping, single-point-of-failure mitigation, dual sourcing/tooling, business continuity playbooks.
- Data & reporting: dashboards for FPY, DPPM, escapes, NCR/CAPA aging, Cp/Cpk; automated alerts for trends and thresholds.

We have an ambitious mission and need excellent people in all our teams - AI research, operations, advanced materials, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering and manufacturing.

Role Overview
Orbital's AI software platform, CurieOS, is used by scientists and engineers to design and build products serving critical industries. Powering this software are our world leading AI models in advanced materials, hardware engineering and simulation.
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Orbital you will deliver CurieOS into customer environments hands-on, writing production code, designing architectures, building integrations and solving problems across the full breadth of industrial R&D. You will embed with customer teams, translate ambiguous high-value problems into working systems, and build solutions that become part of how their scientists and engineers work day-to-day.
First and foremost, we want to work with someone with a love of craftsmanship, continual learning and building systems that scale.
Key Responsibilities
Deliver deployments hands-on, across the breadth of industrial R&D
- Deliver complex customer deployments hands-on, writing production code, designing architectures, building integrations and debugging issues across CurieOS and customer systems
- Design and build systems that connect heterogeneous software, data and physical infrastructure, from simulation campaigns and digital twins to lab instruments, test rigs and CAD/PLM systems
- Build solutions that become embedded in how customer scientists and engineers work day-to-day
Build and deploy
- Embed with customer teams to understand ambiguous, high-value R&D problems, challenge assumptions and identify where CurieOS can deliver meaningful impact
- Translate those problems into a technical approach, milestones and acceptance criteria, making pragmatic architecture and scope trade-offs as you learn
- Build evaluation loops with customer scientists and engineers, defining workflow-specific benchmarks and acceptance criteria that prove the system works in their world
- Own your engagement from initial technical discovery through implementation, production deployment and adoption, including technical quality
- Track KPIs per engagement (screening throughput, design-cycle reduction, experiments avoided) and communicate progress and outcomes to customer stakeholders
Learn and adapt

- Codify successful approaches into reusable integration patterns, tooling and playbooks so every engagement makes the next one faster
- Feed field signal to the platform engineering team to shape the CurieOS roadmap
What We’re Looking For
- Strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of independently building, shipping and operating production software
- A track record of succeeding in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where requirements evolve through direct iteration with users
- The ability to move fluidly between conversations with customer scientists and engineers and deep technical implementation work
- Experience deploying software into complex production environments
- A genuine interest in building software that enables breakthrough scientific and industrial applications

title: Research Scientist, Materials Characterization
text:
About Periodic Labs

About the Role
Join a world-class team of scientists and engineers pushing the boundaries of materials research in a groundbreaking lab where AI and automation unlock discoveries at unprecedented speed and scale. As a Research Scientist within the Periodic Labs experimental effort, you bring AI predictions into reality through physics and measurement science. In this role, you will both develop new material characterization approaches and be part of the team developing autonomous discovery loops.
This is a senior, hands-on role. You will own the design and execution of high-fidelity property measurements, drive the development of high-throughput characterization schemes, and collaborate closely with AI, automation, and materials science teams to build feedback loops that accelerate discovery. You will set the standard for measurement quality and data integrity across the lab.
What You’ll Do
- Develop and perform high-fidelity thermodynamic, transport, and spectroscopic measurements of materials, including electronic, magnetic, and thermal properties
- Design and implement rapid property measurement schemes to scale up the material characterization process and feed AI-guided discovery pipelines
- In collaboration with the AI team, implement automated data analysis and reasoning pipelines for screened materials; contribute to feedback loop design between measurement and prediction
- In collaboration with the engineering team, develop autonomous systems for property characterization leveraging robotics and programmable instrumentation
- Evaluate, procure, and commission new instrumentation; develop custom measurement setups where commercial solutions are insufficient
- Define and enforce data standards, metadata schemas, and documentation practices to ensure measurement outputs are reproducible and reusable
- Uphold and contribute to lab safety standards, particularly around cryogenic systems, high-field magnets, and hazardous materials
You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have

What You’ll Do

- Troubleshoot and diagnose equipment issues across the lab — dispensing heads, reaction chambers, characterization tools — and drive root-cause investigations to durable fixes

- Run design of experiments (DOE) to identify which recipe and process factors most impact outcomes, and use structured methodologies to converge efficiently

You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have

title: Process Technician, Thin Films
text:
About Periodic Labs
Periodic Labs is building an autonomous laboratory for high-throughput materials discovery. Our work combines advanced chemistry, robotics, automation, AI, and materials science to accelerate scientific discovery while maintaining high standards of environmental, health, and process safety.
About the Role
Periodic Labs is building AI that can both simulate science and verify its own predictions. Verifying those predictions experimentally requires a lab that runs reliably - qualified tools, samples prepared to spec, and data logged the same way every time.
We are standing up a dedicated thin-film lab in Menlo Park with a suite of deposition and characterization tools, and are hiring a Process Technician to own day-to-day tool operation, sample preparation, and first-line maintenance. This is the role that keeps throughput high and variance low: you run the SOPs, you cut and prep the coupons, you keep the tools in spec, and you partner with process engineers when an experiment calls for something outside the standard flow.
This is a contract position, on-site, with the possibility of extension or conversion as the lab scales.
What You'll Do
- Run deposition tools to SOP. Execute recipes on vacuum-based thin-film deposition systems. Load and unload, verify chamber state and process conditions, confirm the run matched setpoints, and log the result.
- Prepare samples. Dice and cleave coupons from full wafers; handle mounting and cross-section prep for imaging. Clean and prep substrates per workflow-specific recipes — wet cleans, oxide strip, dehydration bake, substrate and source conditioning.
- Operate characterization tools. Collect and log structural, optical, and electrical film data. Recognize when a scan, fit, or image indicates a tool problem rather than a material result, and escalate rather than re-run blind.
- Perform first-line and preventive maintenance. Chamber opens and cleans, source and consumable changes, shield and liner swaps, pump-down and leak checks, calibration checks, and PM scheduling. Work with vendors and facilities on service visits and keep maintenance history complete.
- Keep the tools qualified. Run qual and monitor samples on a set cadence, track thickness, uniformity, and rate against baseline, and flag drift early. Maintain SPC-style charts where they exist and help build them where they don't.
- Support non-standard work. When engineers need a one-off — an unusual stack, an off-recipe parameter sweep, a new substrate geometry, an unproven prep sequence — you help scope what the tool can safely do, run it, and document what actually happened.
- Document everything. Every run is a potential data point for our models. Record what you did rather than what the recipe said, capture failures and fixes alongside successes, and meet the metadata standards our data pipeline depends on.
- Own lab safety and housekeeping. Chemical handling and waste, gas and precursor changes, lockout/tagout, cleanroom protocol and gowning discipline, and spares and consumables inventory - including at partner facilities we use during ramp.
You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have
- 3+ years of hands-on experience operating thin-film deposition and/or metrology equipment in a semiconductor fab, R&D line, or equipment supplier environment. You have spent real time at a tool, not adjacent to one.
- Working knowledge of at least one deposition technique at the level of practical detail: what a bad pump-down looks like, when a source needs conditioning, why a recipe that ran fine last week is now off-rate.
- Sample prep skill with delicate materials — dicing or cleaving, mounting, cross-sectioning, and cleaning without introducing artifacts.
- Comfort with basic metrology data: reading a thickness map, sanity-checking a film measurement, spotting delamination or particles in an image.
- Mechanical aptitude and hands-on maintenance instinct. You are comfortable inside a chamber, with fittings and fasteners, and with following a service procedure precisely.
- Rigorous documentation habits and attention to detail. You understand why "what I intended" and "what I did" are different records.
- Cleanroom experience and full respect for protocol, chemical safety, and contamination control.
- The ability to work independently, prioritize across several engineers' requests, and escalate anomalies early.
Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have
- Associate degree or technical certificate in a related field, or equivalent military or industry training.
- Experience in a high-mix, low-volume R&D environment where the recipe changes daily and no two lots are identical.
- Vacuum system troubleshooting, RF matching and plasma tuning, or mass flow and pressure control calibration.
- Experience with LIMS, MES, or other systems for tracking samples, runs, and characterization results, and the instinct to treat logging as part of the experiment.
- Wafer-level metrology experience: thickness and resistivity mapping, stress and warpage, at wafer scale rather than coupon scale.
- Familiarity with in-situ or real-time process monitoring during deposition.
- Prior work at university nanofabrication facilities or shared cleanrooms, including facility safety training and tool reservation systems.
Mechanics

title: ML Research Engineer
text:
The Role
Our scientific agent decides what experiment to run next. This role builds the machinery that lets us understand, evaluate, and continuously improve the agent's decisions.
You will work closely with the Principal Scientist to turn hypotheses about agent behavior into reproducible experiments and production improvements. Your initial focus will be evaluation datasets, replay, trajectory analysis, and the policies governing how the agent plans, responds to results, and recovers from failure.
You will own the evaluation and experimentation systems, contribute research ideas, and carry promising changes from prototype through production in partnership with platform engineers.
The profile is engineering-first, ML-strong, and research-capable. You should be as comfortable designing a data schema and CI pipeline as turning an ML or scientific idea into a controlled experiment and shipping the resulting improvement.
What You'll Work On
- Research and experimentation: work with the Principal Scientist to formulate hypotheses about agent behavior, design controlled experiments, and implement and evaluate improvements to planning, tool use, and decision-making.
- Reproducible replay: reconstruct historical agent runs from recorded context so models, prompts, and policies can be compared under consistent conditions, with clear limits on what those comparisons establish.
- Versioned evaluation datasets: curated task sets, splits, and ground truth that evolve without invalidating past results
- Evaluation harness and metrics: decision quality, task success, recovery from error, cost, and latency, with honest treatment of noise and small sample sizes
- Trajectory analysis: instrument agent runs, characterize failure modes, and convert recurring failures into regression coverage
- Control policies: prototype, test, and ship the logic that decides when the agent revises an approach, pivots, escalates to a scientist, or terminates
- Experiment infrastructure: data pipelines, artifact and dataset versioning, experiment tracking, and the tooling that lets the team run a clean comparison in minutes rather than days
- Close partnership with our scientists and platform engineers to connect agent behavior to what actually happens in the Workcell
What We're Looking For
Required:
- 4-8 years building production ML systems, research infrastructure, or data-intensive backends; strong enough to design, build, and ship end-to-end
- Excellent Python and strong software engineering discipline: testing, typing, packaging, code review, CI
- Direct experience with ML evaluation and experimentation: offline evaluation harnesses, dataset and split design, metric design, and sound reasoning about noisy or underpowered results
- Data pipeline skills: schema design, versioning, orchestration (Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, Ray, or equivalent), object storage
- A reproducibility instinct: pinned environments, seeded runs, versioned artifacts, results that hold up when someone else reruns them six months later
- The ability to take ambiguous system behavior, reduce it to a controlled experiment, and write up what the result does and does not support
- Ability to turn ideas into working prototypes quickly, then harden successful ones into reliable production systems
- Initiative and ownership in an environment where the roadmap is still being written
Nice to have:
- Experience with LLM agents: tool calling, planning loops, context management, trajectory logging, and agent evaluation
- Background in sequential decision making: bandits, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, or off-policy evaluation
- Experiment tracking, agent observability, and artifact versioning tools (Langfuse, MLflow, Weights and Biases, DVC)
- Scientific computing, or experience with materials, chemistry, or instrument data
- Experience operating large-scale inference systems, including GPU scheduling and distributed execution
- Observability experience (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog)
- Prior work in lab automation, robotics, or a self-driving lab
What Success Looks Like
In your first six to twelve months:
- Representative historical agent runs can be replayed against recorded context and compared with candidate models, prompts, or policies, with clear limits on those comparisons.
- A versioned evaluation suite gates changes to the agent, and the team trusts it enough to act on the result
- Recurring failure modes are documented, categorized, and covered by regression tests.
- Scientific and agent hypotheses can be turned into controlled experiments quickly, with clear conclusions about what the evidence supports and what to try next.
- At least one meaningful agent or control improvement is shipped to production, with measured gains in decision quality or scientific throughput.

title: Software Engineer, Full Stack

title: Software Engineer, Core Infrastructure
text:

We're looking for a senior Software Engineer to own the core infrastructure behind our self-driving lab: the execution planner that orchestrates the physical lab, the backend services and APIs that manage its data, and the compute infrastructure that powers our agents and scientific simulations. title: Product Designer
text:
About Tetsuwan Scientific
Few fields touch human life as directly as biology does. But the pace of biological research is limited by how slowly and inconsistently experiments can be run by hand. We're building the infrastructure to make experimentation faster, more reproducible, and available to any scientist with questions worth asking.
For decades we've had incredible robotic tools capable of executing experiments without countless tiring hours of pipetting by hand and these instruments are more precise and accurate than manual methods. However, the engineering and validation time required for automating these machines means they are rarely used with the exception of the most repetitive, high throughput research tasks.
Our team has built a user-friendly editor and compiler that ingests a scientist's protocol description, converts it into a structured high-level format, and then automatically compiles it into executable code for these robots. See a demo here: https://tinyurl.com/mrx63phb
We're a small team in San Francisco, currently raising our seed round and growing quickly. Joining now means shaping the product, the team, and the company at a stage where your decisions matter.
The Role
You'll be the first dedicated product designer on the team, working alongside our current designer (who has been splitting design work with engineering), software engineers, automation engineers, and the founders. The right person will grow into owning design end-to-end.
Part of our philosophy is to surface every editable detail to the scientist, so they retain full control over how decisions are made from pdf protocol to code. This poses a major design challenge. Surfacing this level of control to the users while making the UI a pleasant experience means we need to design novel interfaces to communicate lab automation to scientists.
You will be tackling problems with few points of comparison, doing user research, shaping the information architecture, designing the interface, and watching real scientists use what you make.
Qualifications
- You have 3+ years professional experience designing software products
- You can run a project end-to-end: research, sketches, prototypes, polished UI, and a clean handoff to engineers
- Fluency in Figma and adjacent tools
- You're comfortable with multi-discipline technical complexity. You should want to talk to our engineers and learn from our scientists
Nice to Have
- Experience designing for the life sciences, lab workflows, or any technical domain where the user is an expert in something you're not.
- Familiarity with dev-tool or visual programming tools: projectional editors, node graph tools, program state visualization, errors and diagnostics.
- Startup or small-team experience, especially earlier stage.
- Familiarity with frontend work and the interplay between design and technical trade-offs
- A side practice — illustration, motion, printmaking, ceramics, anything that means you make things for the love of it.
Logistics
- Location: San Francisco, in-person at our office in SoMa.
- Compensation: $120K – $160K · Offers Equity
- Process: intro call → portfolio review and design conversation → onsite with the team including a paid design exercise → references → offer.

title: Software Engineer
text:
About Tetsuwan Scientific
Few fields touch human life as directly as biology does. But the pace of biological research is limited by how slowly and inconsistently experiments can be run by hand. We're building the infrastructure to make experimentation faster, more reproducible, and available to any scientist with questions worth asking.
For decades we've had incredible robotic tools capable of executing experiments without countless tiring hours of pipetting by hand and these instruments are more precise and accurate than manual methods. But the engineering and validation time required to automate them means they're rarely used outside of the most repetitive, high-throughput research tasks.
Our team has built a user-friendly editor and compiler that ingests a scientist's protocol description, converts it into a structured high-level format, and then automatically compiles it into executable code for these robots. See a demo here: https://tinyurl.com/mrx63phb
We're a small, quickly growing team based in San Francisco. Joining now means shaping the product, the team, and the company at a stage where your decisions matter.
The role
You'll be joining a team of three software engineers, an automation engineer, and working directly with the founders and our designer. The monorepo codebase spans a compiler (OCaml), backend services (Python), and a protocol editor (TypeScript/React) and we expect you to grow into working across the full stack.
Our engineering challenges go well beyond a typical web app or agent system, involving compiler design and the messy quirks of physical lab hardware. Turning a freeform scientific protocol into reliable robot instructions is a complex interdisciplinary problem with a mixture of context sensitive language problems, tacit knowledge embedded in domain experts, and hard optimization problems with fault intolerant and right-the-first time constraints that necessitate deterministic correctness.
You will be tackling problems with few points of comparisons, deciding how to model them, shipping it, and watching real scientists use what you make.
Qualifications
- 3+ years building software professionally
- You have demonstrated experience taking fuzzy ambiguous problems and turning them into working shipped features independently
- Comfortable jumping between languages and parts of the stack. We don't expect you to know OCaml on day one, but we do expect you to be the kind of person who'd be excited to pick it up
- You have strong opinions about code, held loosely. You should want to leave the codebase better than you found it while balancing engineering momentum
- You like working in-person with a small team where the line between product and engineering is blurry
Nice to have
- Experience or interest in domain specific languages, language design, and projectional editors
- Background in the life sciences, lab automation, or software work in any domain where the user is an expert in something you're not.
- Experience with OCaml, or with other ML-family languages (Haskell, F#, Rust's type system, etc.)
- Experience with Next.js, Tailwind, FastAPI, NeonDB, & Zustand
- Experience or interest in compilers, interpreters, heuristic algorithms and optimizing systems, especially unconventional and domain specific tools
- Familiarity with LLM-in-the-loop systems: parsing, structured extraction, evals
- Startup or small-team experience, especially earlier stage.
Logistics
- Location: San Francisco, in-person at our office in SoMa.
- Compensation: $140K – $180K · Offers Equity
- Process: intro call → take-home project → follow up technical conversation → onsite technical interview → offer.
